title: Galbi
subtitle: Grilled marinated beef short ribs
excerpt: Galbi are Korean grilled beef short ribs, cross-cut through the bone and marinated in soy sauce, Asian pear, garlic, and sesame oil. The marinade tenderises the meat and creates a deep caramelised crust on the grill.
sourceNotes: Galbi, also written 'kalbi', is one of the most celebrated Korean grilled meats. The cross-cut or 'flanken' style of cutting through multiple rib bones is a Korean butchery technique that allows the marinade to penetrate the meat quickly. Galbi is central to Korean barbecue culture and is commonly served at special occasions and family gatherings.

recipe.freezeNotes: Marinated raw ribs freeze well for up to 2 months. Thaw overnight in the fridge before grilling.
recipe.batchNotes: Scale up the marinade and ribs easily. Grill in batches over very high heat.
recipe.makeAheadNotes: Marinate overnight in the fridge for the best flavour and texture.

glossaryTerms.definition: A method of cutting short ribs across the bone rather than between bones, producing thin strips that include multiple small sections of rib bone. This cut is standard for Korean galbi and allows the marinade to penetrate the meat quickly and the ribs to cook fast over high heat.

A sweet Japanese rice wine used in cooking. It adds a mild sweetness and a slight gloss to marinades and sauces. In Korean galbi marinades it helps produce the caramelised crust characteristic of the dish.

content.text: Galbi takes 35 minutes of active cooking and serves 4, but the ribs need at least 4 hours in the marinade. The
through the bone means the meat cooks fast. You want char on the outside and juicy meat inside.

Ask your butcher for beef short ribs cut in the Korean style, about 1cm thick across the bone. Soak the cut ribs in cold water for 30 minutes before marinating to draw out any blood. Pat completely dry before adding the marinade so it adheres properly. Adding
to the marinade gives the ribs their signature gloss and caramelisation.
Soak the ribs in cold water for 30 minutes to remove excess blood. Drain and pat thoroughly dry with kitchen paper.
Mix together the soy sauce, mirin, sesame oil, sugar, garlic, and ginger to make the marinade. Stir until the sugar dissolves.
Add the ribs to the marinade and turn to coat every surface. Cover and refrigerate for at least 4 hours, or overnight.
Heat a griddle pan or barbecue grill to very high heat. Remove the ribs from the marinade and shake off any excess.
Cook the ribs for 3 to 4 minutes per side until charred and caramelised. The thin cut means they cook quickly.
Transfer to a board. Scatter sesame seeds and spring onions over the top. Serve with steamed rice, kimchi, and lettuce leaves for wrapping.

items.cause: Insufficient marinating time or ribs were too thick
items.fix: Marinate for at least 4 hours. Ask for ribs cut to 1cm thickness. Thicker cuts need a lower heat and longer cooking time.

items.symptom: Marinade burns before ribs are cooked through
items.cause: Too much sugar in the marinade or heat too high
items.fix: Shake off excess marinade before grilling. If using a griddle pan, turn the heat down slightly after the initial sear.

items.cause: The grill was not hot enough when the ribs were added
items.fix: Heat the pan or grill until very hot before adding the ribs. A well-heated surface creates an instant sear that prevents sticking.

content.text: Galbi is a Korean barbecue classic. It is cooked at the table in restaurants. It is also made at home on a griddle. It is served at birthdays and family meals. Wrapping the meat in lettuce with rice is traditional.
